text:
Aleksanteri Kaskimaki collected his first NHL point on Thursday, an assist on Justin Barron's second-period... wait, the goal came late in the first, at 13:49, and it put STL up 2-0 on the way to a 6-2 win over VGK at Enterprise Center. Barron finished with a goal and three assists, and Dylan Holloway scored twice, including the power-play goal that closed the scoring.

The rout flatters STL a little. Expected goals, which measure the quality of each chance, came out nearly even: STL 2.94, VGK 2.72. VGK also held a 63-52 edge in shot attempts and outhit STL 36-13. Over a thousand simulated replays of every shot, STL wins 54 percent of the time, so "deserved to win" leans their way, but only slightly. STL took the first period clearly (1.26 expected goals to 0.70), and VGK was the better side in the second (1.36 to 1.02) after Brett Howden cut it to 2-1, though Mason McTavish's tip-in at 8:30 made it 3-1.

Jack Eichel made it 3-2 early in the third, but the game got away from VGK in the next eight minutes. Jimmy Snuggerud scored on a chance worth just 2 percent, and Holloway added another at 10:29. Adin Hill allowed about three goals more than the 31 shots against him should have produced, while Joel Hofer stopped 27 of 29. STL went 2 for 2 on the power play and VGK never had one. The data here doesn't include either team's record or streak, so what the win means for the standings will have to wait.
